article_title: UC San Diego Team Performs First Teleoperated Humanoid Robot Surgery in a Preclinical Trial, Publishing in Nature
summary: Submission approvable with 1 minor warning(s) — file a corrections record on merge

findings.message: Source redirected to different domain: idp.nature.com
Source fetched via Archive.org fallback (original returned 200)
Quoted phrase transposes word order from the source
findings.details: Article body quotes the project page as describing the work as involving "porcine in vivo studies" of laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The project page (source-2, humanoid-surgeon.github.io) actually reads "in vivo porcine studies" in its abstract. The quoted words are reordered rather than reproduced verbatim. Filed as a corrections record entry.

Article body states the Unitree G1 platform identification is "a characterization independently echoed by other outlets covering the study." Of the 6 cited sources, only RobotToday (source-5) identifies the robot as a Unitree G1; none of the other 5 snapshots (UC San Diego Today, Nature, the project page, Medical Xpress, News-Medical) mention "Unitree" or "G1" anywhere. The 'echoed by other outlets' claim is not supported by any source cited in this submission. Filed as a corrections record entry.

content_preview.title: UC San Diego Team Performs First Teleoperated Humanoid Robot Surgery in a Preclinical Trial, Publishing in Nature
content_preview.summary: Engineers and surgeons at UC San Diego used two teleoperated humanoid robots, nicknamed Surgie, to complete two gallbladder-removal procedures, reporting the results in Nature.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Engineers and surgeons at the University of California San Diego say two teleoperated humanoid robots have completed two surgeries during a preclinical trial, a result the university calls a world first, according to [UC San Diego Today](https://today.ucsd.edu/story/surgeons-use-teleoperated-humanoid-robots-to-perform-live-surgery-a-world-first). The work, a collaboration between UC San Diego engineers and surgeons, appears in the July 8 issue of [Nature](https://www.nature.com/arti...

Consider adding trusted domains to config/source_allowlist.txt

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (897 words, within the 400-1200 range) using the standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Prose is clear, attributions are dense and specific, and the 'What We Don't Know' section proactively flags the Nature paywall and cross-outlet disagreement on price/arm-span figures rather than guessing — good editorial hygiene.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 6 source snapshots from sources/2026-07/uc-san-diego-team-performs-first-teleoperated-humanoid-robot-surgery-in-a-preclinical-trial-publishing-in-nature/ via gunzip, verified against manifest.json sha256/status fields. source-0.html.gz (today.ucsd.edu, 200, primary university press release): fully supports the Overview, both surgery descriptions, non-primate mammal detail, Surgie name/dimensions, the 1,800-lbs comparison, and every direct quote from Yip, Thareja, Liu, and Broderick, all reproduced verbatim in the article. source-1.html.gz (nature.com, 200 but redirected_domain idp.nature.com): only a Cloudflare/login challenge page rendered — no article text — consistent with the article's own hedge that the Nature full text is paywalled; the specific facts attributed to this citation (July 8 publication, paper title) are independently corroborated by source-0 and source-2, so no unsupported claim rests solely on this snapshot. source-2.html.gz (humanoid-surgeon.github.io, official project page linked from the UCSD release): confirms the exact paper title, DOI, journal, publication date, and full 10-author list/affiliations used in the article — exact match. However the article's quoted phrase "porcine in vivo studies" transposes the source's actual wording "in vivo porcine studies" (see Content finding above) — filed as a correction. source-3.html.gz (medicalxpress.com, archive_fallback: true, live URL returned 200 but Archive.org snapshot used per script policy): a syndicated republication of the UCSD release; text matches source-0 near-verbatim, corroborating the Surgie name/dimensions and all quotes. source-4.html.gz (news-medical.net, 200): also a close syndication of the UCSD release; corroborates the 1,800-lbs comparison quote attributed jointly to UCSD Today and News-Medical, and all named quotes. source-5.html.gz (robottoday.com, 200): confirms the G1/Unitree identification and the da Vinci $500,000-to-several-million price comparison attributed to RobotToday, both accurate. However, grepped all 6 snapshots for 'Unitree' and 'G1' — only source-5 contains either term. The article's claim that the G1 identification is 'independently echoed by other outlets covering the study' is not supported by any of the article's own 6 cited sources (see Content finding above) — filed as a second correction. Two sources (humanoid-surgeon.github.io, robottoday.com) are not on config/source_allowlist.txt; both are credible for their role here (the study's own official project page, and a robotics trade publication), so this is treated as an allowlist coverage gap rather than a credibility concern.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific I could check against the six cited snapshots checks out: surgery counts/team compositions, animal-subject detail, Surgie's dimensions, the 1,800-lb conventional-system comparison, the da Vinci price range, the Nature paper's title/DOI/author list/affiliations, and all eight direct quotes reproduce their sources verbatim except the two issues noted above (a transposed two-word quote fragment, and an uncited 'echoed by other outlets' claim). Neither issue touches the headline, summary, or lead paragraph.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism; the Analysis section frames portability-vs-precision as an open question rather than asserting a verdict, and correctly notes the trial used animal subjects, not human patients.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/2026-07/ and 2026-06/ for prior coverage of this story or closely related topics. No prior Machine Herald article covers this UCSD/Nature humanoid-surgery study. The closest topical neighbors (23-cmr-surgical-... in 2026-06, 21-johnson-johnsons-ottava-... in 2026-05, 23-nvidia-releases-gr00t-h-... in 2026-03) cover conventional/purpose-built surgical robotics platforms, not humanoid robots performing surgery — a genuinely distinct story and angle.
concerns: Direct quote 'porcine in vivo studies' transposes the source's actual word order ('in vivo porcine studies') — minor but a literal misquote inside quote marks.

The claim that the G1/Unitree identification is 'independently echoed by other outlets covering the study' is not supported by any of the 6 sources cited in this submission; only RobotToday makes that identification among the cited sources.
recommendations: File a corrections record covering both issues (see src/content/corrections/2026-07/12-uc-san-diego-team-performs-first-teleoperated-humanoid-robot-surgery-in-a-preclinical-trial-publishing-in-nature.json).
Consider adding humanoid-surgeon.github.io (official study project pages) and robottoday.com (established robotics trade outlet) to config/source_allowlist.txt for future submissions.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced News piece with two minor, non-lead-affecting inaccuracies (a transposed-word quote and an uncited corroboration claim) that a single corrections record can honestly cover. Approving with corrections rather than rejecting: neither issue touches the headline, summary, or lead, and both are isolated slips rather than a pattern of fabrication.
